body:
Commit 3596c94. Closed the 'no real scalar return-type support' self-hosting gap from NORTHSTAR.md's bootstrap-attempt writeup, scoped precisely to the named case: a #target-bodied defn (length/char-at-shaped) declaring I32/F64/Bool/Unit now emits the correct C type (int/double/int/void) instead of the wrong char* default. Deliberately NOT widened to every I32/F64/Bool-declared defn regardless of body shape -- confirmed live that doing so broke unwrap-or-zero's own pre-existing match/deref-bodied test (real gcc -Werror=int-conversion failure), since emit-i32-boxed/emit-deref still assume a uniform 'everything is char *' convention outside #target bodies, a real, separate, larger gap not attempted here. Also found and fixed a real, previously-dead void check in emit-defn-target-body (compared against 'void' without the trailing space every other branch carries -- never matched anything before now). New test (magic-number) + driver_target_scalar_return.c: real end-to-end assertion, would have failed to even link under the old default. make test: 347/347, all test-selfhost-* targets clean, zero regressions. Remaining self-host gaps named honestly, not closed here: mid-body #target, if-as-whole-body, a narrow struct-literal-shape restriction.

⚓ ☃
title: PARENA self-host: real I32/F64/Bool/Unit scalar return-type support for #target-bodied defns
